newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Algerie ponders relaunch of Paris cargo service.
newsitem.headline: Air Algerie ponders relaunch of Paris cargo service.

text.p: Air Algerie said it was looking forward to re-introducing freighter services between Paris and Algiers if passenger services on the route were resumed.

"Before our services in Paris were suspended in June 1995, we operated two, weekly full-freighter flights on a regular basis between Paris and Algiers, via Oran and Constantine and a charter service between Paris and Hassi-Messaoud using a 20-tonne capacity Hercules L100-30C," a Paris-based Air Algerie cargo official told Reuters.
After the Paris closure, Air Algerie introduced a weekly Hercules freighter flight from Marseille and added a second frequency to an existing Hercules freighter service from Brussels.

"Not being able to offer any cargo lift from Paris has been a serious blow to our freight activities given that for the vast majority of our forwarder customers it is their natural choice of gateway," the official said.
Freight had been trucked to Marseille where the airline had also maintained passenger services and also to Brussels and Lyon.

"This has not been a satisfactory solution especially in Lyon and Marseille where we just don't have enough capacity to ensure a swift transit for freight nor have handling arrangements been adequate. Some of our customers have had to use surface transport for shipments which has entailed a good deal of bureaucracy."

It was not unusual for Air Algerie freight booked on passenger services from Lyon to remain in the warehouse for up to three weeks before being flown out compared to one-week waiting time in Brussels.

"The prospect of three or four round-trip flights a day from Paris to Algiers would ease the situation considerably with Airbus 310 and Boeing 767 passenger aircraft being able to carry between ten and 12 tonnes of palletised freight per flight. However, we still see scope for the resumption of full-freighter services from Paris because this simply suits our customers best and that's what counts. "

The official said if Paris all-cargo flights were restarted, Air Algerie would probably consider reducing its Brussels freighter to one per week and downgrade its weekly Marseille freighter to a fortnightly frequency.

"These plans have yet to be confirmed. Demand for airfreight between France and Algeria is already at a good level and this could strengthen with the resumption of our services. We are therefore leaving our freighter options open."
Recently French and Algerian officials said talks were on course for Air Algerie to provide three or four round-trip flights a day between Paris and Algiers, possibly from April 1.
France ended all flights by French airlines to Algeria after the December 1994 hijacking of an Air France plane in Algiers.
Air Algerie cancelled its flights from Paris in June 1995 following a row with French officials over flight security.

The French authorities had insisted on transferring Air Algerie's operations to an isolated terminal at Paris/ CDG from Paris/Orly. But France has now agreed to move Air Algerie's flights to a regular terminal at CDG and Algeria is keen to resume services in time for the year's summer flight schedules. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
